clips.text_zh: 嘩 SpaceX IPO 第三輪 lockup 9月9號到 期，即係大概 319M 股 (約 7% baseline pool / 2.4% total shares) 突然可以沽。90 個交易日後嘅 major lockup event，到時 supply 衝出來睇下點死 🧐 揸緊 TSLA 都驚被拖累
clips.text_en_b1: On September 9, 2026, about 319 million SpaceX shares become eligible for sale. That is roughly 7% of the baseline pool and about 2.4% of total shares outstanding. This is the 90th trading day after the IPO and the third major lockup release event. Watch supply hit the market.
clips.source_hint: /biz/ thread on SpaceX third lockup release hitting Sep 9, 2026

signal.rationale: Observation post on lockup supply event, no actionable trade setup

clips.text_en_b2: On September 9, 2026, roughly 319 million SpaceX shares become eligible for sale, representing about 7% of the baseline pool and roughly 2.4% of total shares outstanding. This third major lockup release lands on the 90th trading day after the IPO, meaning a sudden wave of supply will likely flood the market. While bulls argue demand can absorb it, anyone holding Tesla should brace for potential drag from a related-party sell-off.
clips.text_en_c1: Approximately 319 million SpaceX shares are set to become eligible for trading on September 9, 2026, representing around 7% of the baseline pool and 2.4% of total shares outstanding. This marks the third major lockup release since the IPO, triggered precisely 90 trading days after listing. Such a sudden surge in circulating supply will inevitably exert downward pressure on the stock, particularly if secondary-market demand fails to absorb the overhang. Tesla holders, whose fortunes remain intertwined with SpaceX's valuation, should brace for potential contagion effects should sentiment deteriorate.
clips.text_en_c2: On the ninth of September 2026, the third major lockup expiry stemming from the SpaceX IPO unfreezes roughly 319 million shares for resale. This tranche, constituting approximately seven percent of the baseline pool and a comparatively modest 2.4 percent of total shares outstanding, will descend upon a market whose appetite remains untested. The release, occurring precisely ninety trading days post-listing, constitutes the most consequential supply shock since the original offering. Should demand fail to absorb the overhang with conviction, secondary prices face predictable gravitational pressure. Holders of correlated equities, notably TSLA, ought to brace for collateral drag as sentiment cascades. Watch the bid-ask spread, watch the volume profile, and, crucially, watch the prevailing appetite.

clips.text_zh: 10年 hold 一樣，你揸 BTC 定黃金？黃金我阿媽都識買，但 BTC 每次 pump 完都有人問可唔可以追。我自己 GOLD long + BTC 慢慢入，又係嗰句 — 又係學費 🙏
clips.text_en_b1: If you had to hold only one asset for the next 10 years, would you choose Bitcoin or gold? What makes your choice better than the other? Gold has been around for thousands of years, but Bitcoin is digital, scarce, and global. The community is split, and the debate never ends on /biz/.
clips.source_hint: /biz/ thread comparing Bitcoin and gold as 10-year holds

signal.rationale: Implicit long-BTC bias from a buy-and-hold comparison thread, but no entry timing

clips.text_en_b2: If you had to commit to a single asset for the next decade, would you pick Bitcoin or gold? Gold has weathered thousands of years of human history, yet Bitcoin offers digital scarcity and a borderless settlement layer that no metal can replicate. While /biz/ remains bitterly divided, seasoned holders typically combine a gold long with gradual BTC accumulation, accepting that both positions will probably cost tuition money along the way.
clips.text_en_c1: Were one compelled to select a single asset for the next decade, the perennial Bitcoin-versus-gold debate offers no easy resolution. Gold, whose store-of-value credentials span millennia, remains intuitively accessible and requires no technological literacy. Bitcoin, by contrast, promises digital scarcity and borderless settlement, yet its volatility has historically tested even the most steadfast conviction. The community remains bitterly divided, and every rally reignites accusations that latecomers are chasing tops. Personal portfolios combining a gold long with gradual Bitcoin accumulation may yet prove the prudent middle path, provided one can stomach the tuition fees along the way.
clips.text_en_c2: Confronted with a hypothetical decade-long moratorium on portfolio rotation, would the discerning investor elect Bitcoin or gold as the singular anchor? Gold, the perennial refuge of monarchs and merchants alike, possesses millennia of empirical validation, yet it remains capital-intensive, geographically tethered, and lamentably indifferent to software. Bitcoin, conversely, is programmable scarcity incarnate, a bearer asset whose settlement rails traverse borders instantaneously, even if its volatility historically precipitates the same forlorn inquiry after every parabolic ascent: surely it cannot be chased at such valuations. The contrarian posture, evidently, is to maintain gold as the primary long while accumulating BTC through disciplined dollar-cost averaging, ostensibly a perpetual exercise in tuition rather than triumph. The debate, eternally inconclusive, persists with religious fervour across /biz/, where conviction is invariably more abundant than capital.

clips.topic_en: Are paid AI models worth it?
clips.text_zh: 死窮鬼共鳴 — /g/ 啲人成日叫人 buy ChatGPT / Claude paid tier，但 Kimi / GLM / Qwen 平 90% 價錢做到 90% 嘢。AI 嚟搶我哋飯碗就話仲慘啲，連訂閱都畀人割 🧐 揾錢優先 ok
clips.text_en_b1: Have you noticed this kind of post? 'If you have not tried the PAID models, you do not know what they are capable of. You have to try the PAID tier of ChatGPT or Claude.' But nobody recommends cheaper models like Kimi, GLM, or Qwen, which deliver about 90% of the performance for maybe 10% of the price. Real spending hack.
clips.source_hint: /g/ thread questioning why everyone pushes paid AI tiers over cheap Chinese models

signal.rationale: Tech discussion on AI model pricing, no trade

clips.text_en_b2: On /g/ you constantly see posts insisting that without trying the paid tiers of ChatGPT or Claude, you simply cannot grasp what modern AI is capable of. Yet virtually nobody recommends cheaper alternatives like Kimi, GLM, or Qwen, which deliver roughly 90% of the performance for around 10% of the price. If AI is supposedly coming for our jobs, the least we can do is stop subsidising premium subscriptions we do not need.
clips.text_en_c1: A familiar refrain echoes across /g/: those who have never sampled the paid tiers of ChatGPT or Claude cannot fathom their true capabilities, the argument goes, and subscriptions are therefore deemed non-negotiable. Yet conspicuously absent from such recommendations are alternatives such as Kimi, GLM, and Qwen, which deliver roughly ninety percent of the performance at a fraction of the cost, perhaps ten percent of the prevailing subscription price. Should artificial intelligence ultimately displace our livelihoods, being systematically fleeced by subscription fees would prove a particularly bitter irony. Prioritising one's earnings remains, on balance, the saner course.
clips.text_en_c2: A persistent orthodoxy pervades certain AI discourse, whereby the uninitiated are admonished that comprehension of frontier capability is contingent upon subscribing to ChatGPT or Claude's premium tier. The proposition, while not entirely without merit, exhibits a curious myopia: models like Kimi, GLM, and Qwen routinely deliver perhaps ninety percent of the performance at a tenth of the financial outlay. For impecunious autodidacts, this represents not merely a budgetary optimisation but a categorical refutation of the received wisdom. Should artificial intelligence ultimately appropriate the breadwinning occupations of the cognitively displaced, the indignity is compounded by subscription servitude to the very instruments of displacement. The pragmatic calculus is straightforward. Preserve liquidity, maximise utility per dollar expended, and refrain from purchasing prestige. The unpaid tiers suffice; the premium tier is largely conspicuous consumption masquerading as intellectual infrastructure.

clips.text_zh: omg 21間美國銀行一齊出 stablecoin，特朗普擺明賣咗美國畀私人公司同 bank。Apple Coin / Tesla Coin / X Coin 全部嚟，US financial market 會被幾百種 digital cash 淹沒 🧐 BTC 仲有得諗，alts 就死硬
clips.text_en_b1: 21 U.S. banks plan to launch a joint stablecoin. This is the real purpose behind Trump's stablecoin bill. He has sold out the U.S. to private companies and banks. Soon you will see Apple Coin, Google Coin, Microsoft Coin, Tesla Coin, X Coin, and Bank Coin flooding the financial markets.
clips.source_hint: /pol/ thread on 21 US banks planning a joint stablecoin under Trump's bill

signal.rationale: News commentary on US stablecoin policy, no direct trade

clips.text_en_b2: Twenty-one U.S. banks have reportedly banded together to launch a joint stablecoin, confirming what sceptics warned about all along: Trump's stablecoin bill effectively handed the American financial system to private corporations. Expect a tidal wave of branded tokens hitting the market, from Apple Coin and Google Coin to Tesla Coin and X Coin. While Bitcoin may weather the storm, altcoins are almost certainly doomed as hundreds of digital cash variants cannibalise liquidity.
clips.text_en_c1: Twenty-one American banks have coalesced around a joint stablecoin initiative, ostensibly fulfilling the latent objective of Trump's recently enacted stablecoin legislation. Critics contend that the administration has effectively ceded American monetary sovereignty to private financial institutions, whose interests seldom align with those of ordinary citizens. The proliferation appears relentless: Apple Coin, Google Coin, Microsoft Coin, Tesla Coin, X Coin, and assorted Bank Coins threaten to inundate domestic markets with hundreds of competing digital currencies. Amid this saturated landscape, Bitcoin retains a credible thesis, whereas altcoins face existential jeopardy.
clips.text_en_c2: An ostensibly innocuous consortium of twenty-one American banking institutions has announced a jointly issued stablecoin, ostensibly to compete within the burgeoning digital payments landscape, though the underlying political economy warrants considerably more scrutiny. Critics contend that the preceding stablecoin legislation constitutes a transparently transactional instrument whereby the erstwhile sovereign prerogative of currency issuance has been effectively ceded to private capital. The downstream consequences, it is feared, will manifest as a Cambrian explosion of tokenised instruments, with corporate entrants such as Apple, Google, Microsoft, Tesla, X, and assorted banking conglomerates each proffering proprietary digital cash. Such proliferation would inevitably dilute the informational signal of any individual stablecoin, fragmenting liquidity and corroding monetary coherence. For Bitcoin maximalists, the thesis remains viable; for altcoin enthusiasts, however, the prognosis is rather more grim. Caveat emptor.

clips.text_zh: lol 騰訊真係細 — 開始 mass report 同落架嘅 Genshin Impact 影片，連 Honda Mariko (Sandrone 聲優) 嘅 stream 都被人 spam 叫佢轉去玩 Wuthering Waves。Tencent 連聲優都搞，呢間公司真係毒 🧐 我繼續食瓜
clips.text_en_b1: The Asian gaming world is rocked by drama as Tencent has started mass reporting and taking down videos and streams about Genshin Impact. In the most notorious case, Honda Mariko, the JP voice actor for Sandrone and streamer, was harassed, her stream was spammed with insults and demands to play Wuthering Waves instead.
clips.source_hint: /v/ thread on Tencent takedown campaign against Genshin Impact content
clips.text_en_b2: The Asian gaming scene is in uproar after Tencent allegedly began mass-reporting Genshin Impact content across social platforms, triggering a wave of takedowns. The most egregious case involves Honda Mariko, the Japanese voice actress for Sandrone, whose livestream was bombarded with spam demanding she promote Wuthering Waves instead. Targeting voice actors crosses a line, and while the popcorn keeps flowing, this kind of corporate thuggery poisons the entire industry.
clips.text_en_c1: The Asian gaming sphere finds itself embroiled in yet another corporate skirmish, as Tencent reportedly orchestrates mass-reporting campaigns aimed at suppressing Genshin Impact-related content across video platforms. Streams promoting the title have been targeted with takedown notices, while prominent creators face coordinated harassment. Most infamously, Honda Mariko, the Japanese voice actress portraying Sandrone, endured sustained stream spam during a recent broadcast, with viewers relentlessly demanding she pivot to Wuthering Waves instead. That a conglomerate would stoop to intimidating individual performers speaks volumes about the company's questionable tactics. Spectators shall continue enjoying the spectacle from a safe distance.
clips.text_en_c2: The Asian gaming industry finds itself once again embroiled in a controversy whose pettiness is matched only by its persistence. Tencent, allegedly unsettled by the continued commercial ascendancy of Genshin Impact, has reportedly orchestrated coordinated mass-reporting campaigns designed to suppress promotional content, thereby precipitating the algorithmic takedown of innocuous videos and streams. The most egregious incident, however, involves Honda Mariko, the Japanese voice actress embodying Sandrone, whose otherwise innocuous livestream was subjected to orchestrated harassment demanding her immediate defection to Wuthering Waves. Such tactics, targeting talent rather than the product itself, betray a corporate culture whose competitive instincts have curdled into something altogether more toxic. The broader competitive landscape, meanwhile, continues to function as intended: competitors compete, audiences spectate, and schadenfreude remains the lingua franca of the consumer. The show, regrettably, goes on.

clips.text_zh: 睇完好自閉 — 405lbs bench press 真係咁都有人做。我仲喺度諗 1pl8 OHP 幾時得，肥仔信都笑我細 🙃 返屋企即刻 push day
clips.text_en_b1: How often do you actually see a 405 lbs bench press in your gym? Most people never see one in their entire lifting career. It takes years of consistent training, proper programming, and good nutrition. When a 405 bencher walks in, the whole gym notices.
clips.source_hint: /fit/ thread asking how often people witness a 405 lbs bench press
clips.text_en_b2: Spotted a 405 lbs bench press in the wild today, and it genuinely hit different. Most lifters train for years without ever witnessing that number loaded onto a bar, since hitting it demands consistent programming, disciplined nutrition, and frankly, decent genetics. Meanwhile I am still grinding away at a single-plate overhead press, feeling absolutely dwarfed by the bigger guys. Time to head home and crank out a serious push day.
clips.text_en_c1: A genuine 405-pound bench press sighting remains a rare phenomenon within commercial gym environments, one that the vast majority of lifters never witness across an entire training career. Attaining such a milestone typically demands years of disciplined programming, meticulous nutritional adherence, and physiological fortune. Meanwhile, intermediate trainees fixate on considerably humbler objectives, such as conquering a single-plate overhead press, achievements that seasoned veterans might dismiss with amusement. Nevertheless, witnessing elite performance firsthand possesses an undeniable galvanising effect, invariably compelling observers to recalibrate their own training intensity upon returning home.
clips.text_en_c2: How frequently does one genuinely witness a 405-pound bench press executed with technical adequacy? For the overwhelming majority of dedicated lifters, the answer remains a rather dispiriting never, despite years of meticulous programming, nutritional discipline, and the gradual accumulation of incremental strength. The achievement, ostensibly prosaic, represents a milestone whose considerable difficulty is inversely proportional to its apparent mundanity. Observing such a lifter saunter casually into the facility while lesser mortals still deliberate the merits of a single plate overhead press produces an almost existential disquiet, compounded by the gentle derision of portly colleagues whose own aspirations remain similarly modest. The appropriate response, however, is neither capitulation nor envy, but rather the immediate commencement of one's prescribed push session, executed with renewed conviction. The iron, as ever, awaits.
